title: Revolute lever: assemble, drive and measure real component motion
intent: Build a two-component mechanism, locate its face-centre joint with clearance, then prove that driving the joint changes the lever's world geometry while preserving its solid volume.
preconditions: Use a separate empty demonstration design. All lengths are mm and all angles are degrees.
Preflight the complete ops list, execute it as one Fusion batch, and retain its returned entity IDs. Names label the example; they are not entity IDs.
lessons: new_component produces an occurrence containing the solid. A body alias addresses the body, not the occurrence; retain created IDs and use the joint's between row or a refreshed tee_scene_summary to identify the occurrences for measurement.
A planar-face joint uses the selected face's centre. This is a central lever pivot, not an arbitrary point or edge joint. The 60 by 12 rectangle exposes rotation that a circular disc would conceal.
The requested joint value is a claim. Measure the lever occurrence in assembly context before and after motion: a native body's local bounds alone cannot establish that the assembly moved.
A 2 mm gap separates the base top and lever bottom. Check their actual Z extents before accepting the assembly; a joint can be valid while its solids intersect.

For these opposing planar faces, flip:true aligns the face frames so offset:2 produces the measured 2 mm gap. Without the flip, Fusion returned a healthy joint but placed the lever inside the base. Verify actual relative geometry, not the offset value alone.

checks.health: No feature or joint errors/warnings. Every body is solid. Verify actual relative extents and component ownership; counts alone do not pass this recipe.
checks.frame: BBox dimensions above are the created solids' native dimensions. Clearance and motion are measured in the base occurrence's frame. No occurrence is grounded by this typed recipe; do not assume a fixed world transform.

revision.intent: Drive the lever through 45 degrees while preserving the pivot, base and clearance.
revision.check: Resolve {{joint_id}} using bindings before preflight/execution. The joint must read rotation_deg=45. Measure both occurrences before and after, and compare the lever relative to the base. In that frame the lever XY bounds change from [60,12] to [50.911688,50.911688] mm within 0.001 mm; thickness remains 4 mm. The lever remains 2880 mm3, the base remains 9600 mm3, their centre-to-centre distance and 2 mm face clearance remain fixed. Where the base occurrence is unchanged, fu_measure on the lever must directly report [50.911688,50.911688,4] mm. Otherwise transform the geometry into the base frame before comparing. A changed joint value with unchanged relative assembly geometry fails.

motion_probe.check: At 90 degrees the lever bounds in the base occurrence frame must measure [12,60,4] mm with 2880 mm3 volume and unchanged relative centre/clearance. A return to 0 degrees must recover [60,12,4]. Retain every sample, including failures; do not infer the sweep from one readback.

scope: This is a kinematic demonstration, not a load, stress, bearing, fastening or manufacturability validation. It demonstrates a central revolute constraint with clearance; no physical pivot pin or bearing is modelled. The typed lane does not ground either occurrence, so verify relative motion without claiming an anchored world frame.
references: docs/research/71-fusion-lane.md sections 10.5 and 10.6; verified API rows 12, 43-47 and 50
id_resolution: Resolve joint_id from the actual created IDs and details or a refreshed tee_scene_summary. If the kernel trims kind/name as echoes, the returned joint row's between/rotation_deg fields establish the association. The ordered between IDs identify the base and lever occurrences. Never guess j1 or use @pivot in a later batch.
export_check: Choose local absolute output paths and export the whole design, omitting of. Independently read STEP: two solids total 12480 mm3 in the sampled assembly position. Reopen F3D in a separate document and verify the two occurrences and revolute joint; STEP carries geometry, while F3D retains the native mechanism. Entity IDs belong to their document and must be rediscovered after reopening.
